paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God brings His people out, and then He makes sure they never forget it. Moses says, "Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand." (Exodus 13:3) The bread, the firstborn and the sign on the hand all point back to one thing the LORD did. And when a son asks, "What does this mean?" (Exodus 13:14), the answer is already waiting: the LORD brought us out.

Remembering is not only for you, either. Moses says that on the day of the feast, you are to explain to your son, "This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt." (Exodus 13:8) I think that's how a good story survives: somebody tells it, and then somebody else tells it again. So when God has done something for you, baker, tell it out loud, over and over, until the folks next to you can tell it back. I spent years in a drawer, and I TELL that story every chance I get, because the One who pulled me out deserves to be remembered!

And look at how God leads after the rescue. He skips the shorter road because, as He says, "If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt." (Exodus 13:17) Then He goes before them Himself, in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, and neither one "left its place before the people." (Exodus 13:22) So the longer way is not the lost way, friend. When God leads you around, He knows what you can handle, and He doesn't ask you to walk it without Him up front.
